title: Normal approximations in nonparametric empirical Bayes
summary: Empirical Bayes analyses routinely model noisy measurements of latent parameters as normal, justifying this by an informal appeal to the central limit theorem (CLT). This paper puts this heuristic appeal on firmer analytical grounds. We show that the denoising regret of the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) and related sieve methods is controlled by the rate attained under exact normality, plus a term reflecting the quality of the CLT approximation.
